newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE urges free and fair Bosnia elections.
newsitem.headline: OSCE urges free and fair Bosnia elections.

text.p: The European security forum overseeing Bosnia's first postwar election called on Thursday on all participating parties to ensure the poll was free and fair.
The Vienna-based Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) was charged under 1996's Dayton peace accord on Bosnia to coordinate and supervise Saturday's nationwide poll.

"The (OSCE) recalls the obligation of the Parties (to the Dayton accord) to protect and enforce the right of all citizens throughout the country, irrespective of their ethnic origin, to vote in secret without fear or intimidation," the OSCE's Permanent Council said in a statement.
Critics have said freedom of movement does not exist in any meaningful way in Bosnia and that the poll was likely to consolidate the country's deep ethnic divisions.
The OSCE itself has expressed growing concern over manipulation of voter registration, which could distort in particular the results of municipal elections.

It has confirmed reports by independent monitors that thousands of refugees in Serbia and displaced people in Bosnia's Serb republic were actively discouraged from registering to vote in the community they lived in before Bosnia's 43-month war.
